001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
004import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
005import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
006
007/**
008 * A step of the pump's Dexcom CGM session state machine: the session state before (byte 10) and
009 * after (byte 14) the step and the event that caused it (byte 22). Seen on the t:slim X2 and the
010 * Tandem Mobi, with G6 and G7 sessions.
011 *
012 * <p>With no CGM session the pump writes (STOPPED, STOPPED, IDLE_TICK) every 300 s of pump time,
013 * on its own schedule, unrelated to the 5-minute BasalDelivery records. With a session it writes
014 * CYCLE_START once per 5-minute transmitter cycle, then either DATA_RECEIVED immediately before
015 * the {@link DexcomG6CGMHistoryLog} / {@link DexcomG7CGMHistoryLog} reading (same second) or
016 * NO_DATA 27 s after CYCLE_START when no reading arrives. The records continue while insulin
017 * delivery is suspended and stop only while the pump is off.
018 *
019 * <p>Evidence (https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpX2/issues/146): byte 10 equals the previous
020 * record's byte 14 in 15771 of 15774 consecutive pairs on 11 pumps (the exceptions span pump
021 * restarts); byte 14 equals the {@code sessionStateId} of CgmStatusV2Response/CGMStatusResponse
022 * polled by a phone app in 276 of 284 polls on 7 pumps; and 4318 of 4324 five-minute CGM
023 * readings were immediately preceded by a DATA_RECEIVED record.
024 *
025 * <p>This is the CGM session state, not Control-IQ's CGM availability: Control-IQ stops treating
026 * the CGM as available after about 20 minutes without readings while this state stays ACTIVE.
027 * Control-IQ being on or off does not change these records.
028 *
029 * <p>The class name and the state and event names are provisional. Opcode 219 is not in Tandem's
030 * cloud event schema or the Mobi app's history log list, where it is one of two unnamed ids (211
031 * and 219) in the block of Gx CGM records (210-220); it is written for G7 sessions too. Bytes
032 * 11-13, 15-21 and 23-25 were zero in all 20856 records observed and are exposed raw.
033 */
034@HistoryLogProps(
035    opCode = 219,
036    displayName = "CGM State Change"
037)
038public class CgmStateChangeGxHistoryLog extends HistoryLog {
039
040    private int previousStateId;
041    private int stateId;
042    private int eventId;
043    private int unknown11;
044    private int unknown15;
045    private long unknown18;
046    private int unknown23;
047
048    public CgmStateChangeGxHistoryLog() {}
049    public CgmStateChangeGxHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int previousStateId, int stateId, int eventId) {
050        this(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, previousStateId, stateId, eventId, 0, 0, 0, 0);
051    }
052
053    public CgmStateChangeGxHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int previousStateId, int stateId, int eventId, int unknown11, int unknown15, long unknown18, int unknown23) {
054        super(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum);
055        this.cargo = buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, previousStateId, stateId, eventId, unknown11, unknown15, unknown18, unknown23);
056        this.previousStateId = previousStateId;
057        this.stateId = stateId;
058        this.eventId = eventId;
059        this.unknown11 = unknown11;
060        this.unknown15 = unknown15;
061        this.unknown18 = unknown18;
062        this.unknown23 = unknown23;
063    }
064
065    public int typeId() {
066        return 219;
067    }
068
069    /**
070     * <table border="1">
071     * <caption>Parsed fields for CgmStateChangeGxHistoryLog:</caption>
072     * <tr><td><code>previousStateId</code></td><td><code>(int) (word10 &amp; 0xFF)</code></td></tr>
073     * <tr><td><code>unknown11</code></td><td><code>(int) (word10 &gt;&gt;&gt; 8)</code></td></tr>
074     * <tr><td><code>stateId</code></td><td><code>(int) (word14 &amp; 0xFF)</code></td></tr>
075     * <tr><td><code>unknown15</code></td><td><code>(int) (word14 &gt;&gt;&gt; 8)</code></td></tr>
076     * <tr><td><code>unknown18</code></td><td><code>Bytes.readUint32(raw, 18)</code></td></tr>
077     * <tr><td><code>eventId</code></td><td><code>(int) (word22 &amp; 0xFF)</code></td></tr>
078     * <tr><td><code>unknown23</code></td><td><code>(int) (word22 &gt;&gt;&gt; 8)</code></td></tr>
079     * </table>
080     */
081    public void parse(byte[] raw) {
082        Validate.isTrue(raw.length == 26);
083        this.cargo = raw;
084        parseBase(raw);
085        long word10 = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 10);
086        long word14 = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 14);
087        long word22 = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 22);
088        this.previousStateId = (int) (word10 & 0xFF);
089        this.unknown11 = (int) (word10 >>> 8);
090        this.stateId = (int) (word14 & 0xFF);
091        this.unknown15 = (int) (word14 >>> 8);
092        this.unknown18 = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 18);
093        this.eventId = (int) (word22 & 0xFF);
094        this.unknown23 = (int) (word22 >>> 8);
095    }
096
097    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int previousStateId, int stateId, int eventId) {
098        return buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, previousStateId, stateId, eventId, 0, 0, 0, 0);
099    }
100
101    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int previousStateId, int stateId, int eventId, int unknown11, int unknown15, long unknown18, int unknown23) {
102        return HistoryLog.fillCargo(Bytes.combine(
103            HistoryLog.typeIdBytes(219, 0),
104            Bytes.toUint32(pumpTimeSec),
105            Bytes.toUint32(sequenceNum),
106            Bytes.toUint32((previousStateId & 0xFF) | ((long) unknown11 << 8)),
107            Bytes.toUint32((stateId & 0xFF) | ((long) unknown15 << 8)),
108            Bytes.toUint32(unknown18),
109            Bytes.toUint32((eventId & 0xFF) | ((long) unknown23 << 8))));
110    }
111
112    /**
113     * @return raw byte 10: the session state before this step. It equalled the previous record's
114     * {@link #getStateId()} in every observed pair except across pump restarts, which reset the
115     * state to STOPPED without writing a record.
116     */
117    public int getPreviousStateId() {
118        return previousStateId;
119    }
120
121    public State getPreviousState() {
122        return State.fromId(previousStateId);
123    }
124
125    /**
126     * @return raw byte 14: the session state after this step
127     */
128    public int getStateId() {
129        return stateId;
130    }
131
132    public State getState() {
133        return State.fromId(stateId);
134    }
135
136    /**
137     * @return raw byte 22: what caused this step
138     */
139    public int getEventId() {
140        return eventId;
141    }
142
143    public Event getEvent() {
144        return Event.fromId(eventId);
145    }
146
147    /**
148     * @return true if the state changed in this step. Most records repeat the state.
149     */
150    public boolean isStateChange() {
151        return previousStateId != stateId;
152    }
153
154    /**
155     * Zero in every record observed.
156     *
157     * @return raw bytes 11-13 as a little-endian uint24
158     */
159    public int getUnknown11() {
160        return unknown11;
161    }
162
163    /**
164     * Zero in every record observed.
165     *
166     * @return raw bytes 15-17 as a little-endian uint24
167     */
168    public int getUnknown15() {
169        return unknown15;
170    }
171
172    /**
173     * Zero in every record observed.
174     *
175     * @return raw uint32 at offset 18
176     */
177    public long getUnknown18() {
178        return unknown18;
179    }
180
181    /**
182     * Zero in every record observed.
183     *
184     * @return raw bytes 23-25 as a little-endian uint24
185     */
186    public int getUnknown23() {
187        return unknown23;
188    }
189
190    /**
191     * CGM session state. Values 0-2 match the {@code sessionStateId} the pump reports in
192     * CgmStatusV2Response. Value 3 is rare (39 of 20856 records) and was always entered from
193     * START_PENDING on a NO_DATA step while CgmStatusV2Response still reported START_PENDING; its
194     * meaning is unknown, so it maps to UNKNOWN (use the raw id).
195     */
196    public enum State {
197        STOPPED(0),
198        /**
199         * Session started but not yet producing readings. During a long signal loss an ACTIVE
200         * session also drops to this state for one cycle every 30 minutes.
201         */
202        START_PENDING(1),
203        ACTIVE(2),
204        UNKNOWN(-1),
205
206        ;
207
208        private final int id;
209        State(int id) {
210            this.id = id;
211        }
212
213        public static State fromId(int id) {
214            for (State s : values()) {
215                if (s.id == id && s != UNKNOWN) {
216                    return s;
217                }
218            }
219            return UNKNOWN;
220        }
221
222        public int getId() {
223            return id;
224        }
225    }
226
227    /**
228     * What caused a step. Provisional names.
229     */
230    public enum Event {
231        /**
232         * Start of a transmitter cycle: once per 5-minute cycle while ACTIVE, 0-5 s before
233         * DATA_RECEIVED; several in a burst while START_PENDING. Also the event of the
234         * STOPPED to START_PENDING transition when a session starts.
235         */
236        CYCLE_START(1),
237        /**
238         * Transmitter data received. The CGM reading record, when there is one, follows in the
239         * same second.
240         */
241        DATA_RECEIVED(2),
242        /**
243         * No reading this cycle: written 27 s after CYCLE_START while ACTIVE, or on the 5-minute
244         * schedule when the transmitter was not heard at all.
245         */
246        NO_DATA(3),
247        /**
248         * A session command such as a sensor start or stop, transmitter id or G7 pairing code.
249         * Every transition to STOPPED has this event.
250         */
251        SESSION_COMMAND(4),
252        /**
253         * Follows, within 10 s, a pump-button release or (Mobi) a signed control request from a
254         * BLE app. Written only while a CGM is set up; what the pump does at this step is unknown.
255         */
256        USER_ACTIVITY(5),
257        /**
258         * 300-second tick while there is no CGM session.
259         */
260        IDLE_TICK(6),
261        UNKNOWN(-1),
262
263        ;
264
265        private final int id;
266        Event(int id) {
267            this.id = id;
268        }
269
270        public static Event fromId(int id) {
271            for (Event e : values()) {
272                if (e.id == id && e != UNKNOWN) {
273                    return e;
274                }
275            }
276            return UNKNOWN;
277        }
278
279        public int getId() {
280            return id;
281        }
282    }
283}
